# Results -- Study 74 (Mind-the-Gap) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  Overnight gap =
today open minus prior close, expressed as a percent of prior close.  We test two
things: (1) whether the **fill rate** (intraday range includes the prior close) is
above 50% after conditioning on gap size, and (2) whether a **gap-fade backtest** --
enter at the open opposite the gap, symmetric +/-1 ATR(20) take-profit/stop, close
at end-of-day -- beats a random-direction control on the same entries.  Five tickers:
SPY, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA, NVDA.  Daily bars, 10 years (2016-06-14 to 2026-06-12),
auto-adjusted (split + dividends).  As-of **2026-06-12**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | N sessions | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY  | 2016-06-14 -> 2026-06-12 | 2,514 | `4391028341b9` |
| AAPL | 2016-06-14 -> 2026-06-12 | 2,514 | `3c278951d53e` |
| MSFT | 2016-06-14 -> 2026-06-12 | 2,514 | `140b4b4f6da1` |

| NVDA | 2016-06-14 -> 2026-06-12 | 2,514 | `795eddb78bba` |

Pooled N = 12,570 session-days across five tickers.

## Part 1 -- The mechanical fill rate

The claim "gaps always fill" is a conditional-probability claim.  We measure it by
gap-size bucket (small < 0.25%, medium 0.25-1%, large > 1%):

| Bucket | N gaps | N fills | Fill rate | 95% CI (Wilson) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **small** (|gap| < 0.25%) | 3,580 | 3,149 | **87.97%** | [86.9%, 88.9%] |
| **medium** (0.25% to 1%) | 5,537 | 3,582 | **64.69%** | [63.4%, 65.9%] |
| **large** (|gap| > 1%) | 3,445 | 1,296 | **37.62%** | [36.0%, 39.3%] |

**Key finding:** small gaps fill trivially (the intraday range brackets them by noise
alone); medium gaps fill ~65% of the time -- reliably above 50%, a real statistical
finding; large gaps fill only 38% of the time -- *less* than a coin.  The folk claim
"gaps always fill" is therefore half-right: medium gaps tend to fill, but large
news-driven gaps tend *not* to fill on the same day.

The pattern for medium gaps is real: the Wilson CI [63.4%, 65.9%] excludes 50% with
enormous margin.

## Part 2 -- The honest tradable test: symmetric 1:1 ATR barrier

A direction-symmetric payoff (+/-1 ATR take-profit and stop) is the only fair way to
ask "does the fade point the right way?" -- with TP and SL equidistant a coin earns
approximately 0.

| Arm | N | Win-rate | Mean (bps/trade) | Skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Gap-fade (vs prior close dir.)** | 12,444 | 50.61% | **+0.46** | -0.02 | **+0.30** |
| Random direction (control) | 12,444 | 49.16% | -3.81 | -- | -2.28 |

- The fade's gross expectancy is **+0.46 bps/trade**, HAC *t* = **+0.30** --
  statistically **indistinguishable from zero**.  The mechanical gap-fill tendency
  (medium gaps fill 65% of the time) does not translate into a tradable symmetric
  edge.  Why?  The stop (1 ATR) is often wide enough that the 35% of non-fills cost
  more than the 65% of fills earn.
- The fade **does** beat the random-direction coin by **+4.27 bps/trade**, which is
  the correct sign -- the fill tendency is real -- but the fade return itself is not
  statistically distinguishable from zero (HAC *t* = +0.30, nowhere near 2).

### Per-instrument breakdown

| Ticker | N | Win-rate | Mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | 2,494 | 50.7% | +1.44 | +0.99 |
| AAPL | 2,494 | 51.3% | -0.37 | -0.14 |
| MSFT | 2,494 | 50.2% | -1.67 | -0.64 |
| TSLA | 2,478 | 51.8% | +5.06 | +0.98 |
| NVDA | 2,484 | 49.1% | -2.15 | -0.49 |

No single ticker clears the HAC |*t*| >= 2 bar.  SPY is the best at t=+0.99 -- a
positive result but below the inference bar.

## Part 3 -- The cost sweep

With ~1 trade/day per ticker (248/yr), costs compound quickly:

| Round-trip cost | Net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* | Approx annualised |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +0.46 | +0.30 | +1.1%/yr |
| 0.5 bps | -0.54 | -0.35 | -1.3%/yr |
| 1.0 bps | -1.54 | -1.01 | -3.8%/yr |
| 2.0 bps | -3.54 | **-2.31** | **-8.8%/yr** |

The gross edge barely clears zero (t=+0.30), so the break-even cost is effectively
zero: any realistic round-trip cost turns it into a loser.  At 2 bps (plausible for
single-name retail) it is a statistically significant loser.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** The medium-gap fill rate is robustly above 50% (65%, CI
  [63.4%, 65.9%]).  The fill phenomenon is real.  But the *tradable* expression
  of it -- the symmetric fade -- earns only +0.46 bps/trade with HAC *t* = +0.30:
  indistinguishable from noise.  Literature supports the pattern; this tape cannot
  certify a tradable edge => **WEAK**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** A near-zero gross edge means no positive break-even cost
  exists.  At 1 trade/day, any realistic cost (>= 0.5 bps) creates a net loser.
- **Gaps always fill? -- BUSTED for large gaps.** 38% fill rate for large gaps
  demolishes the "always" claim.  Medium gaps fill 65% -- real but not actionable
  at symmetric payoffs.
